title: Pull-Up Button Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A GP14 button circuit with the internal pull-up resistor: toggle the button and the pull-up to see the pin voltage, value() and a floating input.

learningObjectives: Analyze how a pull-up resistor sets the resting voltage of an input pin
Explain why a pressed button reads 0 (active low) with a pull-up
Describe what a floating input is and why it gives random readings
prerequisites: Voltage and current basics from Chapter 2

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

keyQuestions: Why does an unconnected input not simply read 0?
How much current flows through the pull-up when the button is open?
Why does a pressed button read 0?
commonMisconceptions: The pull-up makes the pressed button read 1
The pull-up resistor wastes current all the time
assessmentOpportunities: Students complete the four-row table correctly.
Students use the words "floating" and "active low" correctly in an explanation.
Students explain why no current flows through the pull-up while the button is open.

controls.label: Press button / Release button
controls.description: Closes or opens the push button

controls.label: Internal pull-up (Pin.PULL_UP)
controls.description: Connects or disconnects the internal pull-up resistor
